audit_notes: Slip: for grooves infused with a lubricant more viscous than water (mu_o/mu_w = 3e-3/1.22e-3 = 2.5), the effective slip is strongly reduced relative to the gas-filled case (Schoenecker, Baier & Hardt 2014): b_LIS ~ b_gas/(1 + c mu_o/mu_w) with c ~ 1-2 for groove depth ~ pitch. b_gas (Philip, 20 um pitch, 90% open) = 11.8 um -> b_LIS ~ 11.8/(1+1.5*2.5) = 2.5-3.4 um. Adjusted effective_slip_length 4 um -> 3 um (b+ = 0.56); expected gain 3/98 = 3.1%. Lubricant budget: reservoir 1 mm = 1 L/m2; assumed turbulent shear depletion ~1 um/day (1 mL/m2/day) -> reservoir lasts ~2.7 years if the depletion rate holds; measured depletion in turbulent flow at tau_w ~50 Pa is uncertain by an order of magnitude (lubricant drains faster when not retained by capillarity). Total release ~10 L/day, ~3.6 m3/year per 1e4 m2 hull, continuously discharged into the sea; environmentally acceptable (readily biodegradable ester) lubricants exist (VGP 2013 EAL rules) but this is a continuous discharge. Capillary retention: Laplace pressure 2 gamma_ow/ w ~ 2*0.03/18e-6 = 3.3 kPa, larger than the shear stress on the film (50 Pa) but the film shear-drains along grooves. Structural: 1 mm porous reservoir + textured cap, mechanically soft; hydrostatic pressure balanced by pore connectivity. Baseline: smooth FR without lubricant (slip 0).

performance_gain.label: Skin-friction reduction vs clean FR hull

hard_constraints: lubricant discharge must be reported and minimised
